ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla

facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek
a diffuse, firm, non-tender mass measuring about 4 × 5 cm
extended from the infraorbital region superiorly to the lip commissure inferiorly, medially obliterating the nasal ala, and laterally approaching the preauricular area
well-defined vestibular swelling measuring 4 × 3 cm, extending from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar
Routine hematologic parameters were within normal limits
Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and neck showed a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion in the left premaxillary region
adjacent bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus
a provisional diagnosis of malignancy of the left maxilla was made
differential diagnosis included benign tumor, sarcoma, lymphoma, and melanoma
An incisional biopsy suggested myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla
concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek, a diffuse firm mass, and adjacent bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus on CT, are consistent with a malignant tumor such as squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla.

The patient's presentation with a swelling of the left cheek and a differential diagnosis including lymphoma, along with the biopsy suggestion of lymphoid hyperplasia, could be consistent with a lymphoma of the maxilla.
The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging mass and adjacent bony destruction, along with a differential diagnosis including sarcoma, could be consistent with a sarcoma of the maxilla.
The patient's presentation with a swelling of the left cheek and a differential diagnosis including melanoma, could be consistent with a melanoma of the maxilla, although this would be less common.
The incisional biopsy suggested myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which could be a benign inflammatory condition or a reactive process, and may not necessarily be related to a malignant tumor.

rationales.F06: The CT findings suggest a soft-tissue density lesion, which could be consistent with several types of tumors.
rationales.F07: Bony destruction is more typical of aggressive malignancies.
rationales.F08: A provisional diagnosis of malignancy increases the likelihood of cancerous conditions.
rationales.F10: The biopsy results directly indicate myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, ruling out other options.
